clinical_description: Patient 3 is a clinically healthy 2-year-old child who, at 10 months of age, was diagnosed with mild hypertransaminasemia as an incidental finding. Liver ultrasonography revealed a mild steatosis and the follow-up showed fluctuating values of serum transaminases, and elevated ALP and CK. Other liver tests were normal except antithrombin-III activity of 68% and low ceruloplasmin (8 mg/dL, normal range 20–46).
